input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 14 (p0079) gives Client an unrestricted, no-cause right to terminate at any time by written notice, with services running only to the last day of the month following the notice month (i.e., roughly 30–60 days' wind-down) and no early-termination fee or penalty of any kind. That sits at or above the preferred position on the material terms: a Customer convenience right on short notice with no exit penalty. On the Vendor side, Section 13 (p0078) sets a 1-year term with automatic one-year renewals and gives TrueLink no mid-term termination-for-convenience right at all — its only no-cause exit is a mutual non-renewal notice 30 days before the end of a term, which is an end-of-term exit of the type the fallback expressly tolerates. The early termination of Sections 2 and 3 in p0078 is triggered by Client breach/regulatory loss, not convenience, so it is not a Vendor walk-away right. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: (i) there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, though this is largely moot because fees are invoiced monthly in arrears under Section 5a (p0045); and (ii) the end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than 90 days, but it is symmetric and equally available to us, so it benefits our party as much as the Vendor. No redline proposed.
